newsitem.title: USA: Ohio votes Tuesday on abatements, bonds and levies.
newsitem.headline: Ohio votes Tuesday on abatements, bonds and levies.

text.p: Ohio's special election Tuesday includes six bond referendums ranging from $3 million to nearly $43 million, 25 public school district tax levy requests and two city income tax questions.
Among the other issues on the slate, Cleveland voters will decide if their cash-strapped school district should be excluded when the city grants future property tax abatements to businesses.

The ballot initiative sponsored by the Cleveland Teachers Union faces stiff opposition from the district itself and Mayor Michael White, who contend the abatements are a seldom-used tool that actually increase tax revenues by attracting more businesses.
Under the initiative, the city or a company requesting a new property tax abatement would be required to reimburse the public schools for lost revenues.

Cleveland schools are on Auditor Jim Petro's fiscal emergency list and have been under state control since March 1995. Ohio lawmakers in July approved passing control of the district to the Cleveland mayor.
School districts have sought five of the six bond issues in Tuesday's election. Perrysburg school district near Toledo tops the list, seeking $42.93 million of bonds for school building improvements.
Nordonia Hills schools near Akron have sought $33.5 million of bonds for school site improvements and Plain local schools near Columbus seek $19.89 million for site improvements.

Hamilton city schools seek $11 million of bonds for site improvements to district facilities and Tiffin city schools have asked for $5.6 million of bonds for the district in the north central Ohio community.

City of London southwest of Columbus has also sought $3 million of bonds for road improvements. Middleburg Heights seeks a 0.75 percent local income tax and North College Hill city seeks a 0.45 percent local income tax.
